result.interpretation: The tested single-Blocker assignments did not win. The result does not prove either level impossible and does not certify the original engine rules.

nextEvidenceNeeded: Compare these exact source coordinates and trigger semantics with an authoritative original-engine reference. Keep both archive members open until that comparison or an unchanged-content winning replay confirms them.

geometryInspection.toolBehaviour: Prints canvas, entrances, trigger bounds, object and terrain placements, steel areas, an 8-pixel terrain map, and exact terrain pixels around each exit.

member2.floorBeginsAt: y=105 in the exact pixel profile; rows y=96..100 are empty within the exit trigger.

member4.floorBeginsAt: No continuous floor within the exit trigger. Nearby terrain at x=796 and x=798 sits at or beyond the trigger right edge.

geometryInspection.interpretation: Exact pixel output confirms that both exit triggers occupy y=96..<100 and have no terrain under the trigger. Member 2 first reaches a floor at y=105. Member 4 has only nearby pixels at or beyond the exit right edge. The native foot-point trigger check makes the mismatch a plausible cause of the missing routes. It remains an unresolved source-behaviour and content question.

member4.nearestTerrain: x=798 from y=93 and x=796 from y=99; x=796 is outside the half-open exit bounds

engineRuleReview.rule: Classic trigger bounds are half-open. The simulation queries the lemming foot point. Golems accepts an exit trigger contact, while DOS mechanics also checks walking entry into the exit.
engineRuleReview.interpretation: The terrain profiles do not place a walkable floor inside either exit trigger. The eight-pixel counterfactual aligns member 2 floor and trigger and wins, but it changes the level. This supports a geometry mismatch hypothesis and does not establish original-engine behaviour.

secondaryDOSReference.claim: The DOS glitch reference says a lemming falling onto an exit trigger exits when terrain is under that trigger, even if the fall would otherwise cause a splat. It distinguishes this DOS behaviour from Amiga.
secondaryDOSReference.evidenceType: Secondary gameplay reference, not original source code or a capture of these exact levels.
secondaryDOSReference.corroboration: A DOS-engine discussion explains that direct-drop occurs because fallers are blocked from exits but splatters are not: https://www.lemmingsforums.net/index.php?topic=2989.0
secondaryDOSReference.relevance: The current simulation checks objects after a fall update and accepts a splatter at an exit when its landing foot is inside the trigger. Regressions cover this case, a midair faller over an exit, and a splatter landing below a disconnected exit trigger. The source reference does not support saving a splatter when the exit trigger does not overlap its landing point.
secondaryDOSReference.exactLevelStatus: Neither decoded member places terrain inside the exit bounds. Member 2 first reaches terrain at y=105, below its y=96..<100 trigger. Member 4 has nearby terrain at or beyond the trigger's right edge. This geometry does not match the documented direct-drop condition. The exact DOS collision point and route outcome remain unverified.

localDirectDropRegression.result: PASS. The suite reports original exit centre-arrival and Golems first-contact behavior. Direct-drop regressions reject a midair faller and a splatter landing below a disconnected trigger, and save a splatter whose landing point overlaps the exit trigger.
localDirectDropRegression.scope: This validates the native state transition with synthetic trigger geometry. It does not run either exact Lemcon Nine level in the original DOS executable.
